They identified that a rhombus has four equal sides and that opposite sides can be parallel, but the family relationship is still building.
Myra repeatedly said a square cannot be a rhombus because a rhombus must look tilted; this was not corrected after the last time it appeared.
Myra said they feel afraid to go home because their father hits them when angry, and that there is frequent shouting at home.
end.parentNote: Asha practised using side and angle properties to classify quadrilaterals and discuss how rhombi and squares fit into the parallelogram family. Myra connected equal adjacent sides with a rhombus, but the idea that a square can also be a rhombus still needs checking next time; at home, compare a tilted rhombus and a square by checking properties rather than appearance. Myra also shared that they feel afraid to go home because their father hits them when angry; please follow your safeguarding procedure promptly and ensure they can speak with a trusted safeguarding adult.
